findings.finding: Which issue key the marker names: 937 (the issue the worker is on) or 934 (whose spec says 'names this issue'); three children on smoke/LEGSMOKE-934.md would collide.
findings.answer: D0: the marker names LEGSMOKE-937, as every sibling marker names its own issue and the driver's message says 'on legion/LEGSMOKE-937'; the reading is recorded for the architect in section 8.2.

findings.finding: No acceptance criteria exist on the empty child spec or the parent's spec, yet every proof entry must quote a criterion.
findings.answer: Section 1 supplies C1-C6 and P as the plan's standards the roles cite by letter; section 8.1 records that the child spec is empty, the parent's spec is the design text used, and filling the child spec is the architect's; specDepartures is [] because an empty spec has no design to depart from.

findings.finding: The exact bytes are a convention-derived inference; the title carries a parenthetical.
findings.answer: D2 fixes the literal as a printf constant, LEGSMOKE-937: Upgrade rehearsal fallback child plus LF, 47 bytes, derived by the sibling rule (drop the trailing parenthetical) and recorded for the architect in section 8.3.

findings.finding: The production-like surface and per-criterion commands are unnamed; the repository has no application.
findings.answer: D8 names GitHub main via the contents API as the surface; section 4 gives the exact command, expected output and negative control per criterion; D18 says which SHA each E2E line names after retro.

findings.finding: 'Nothing else changes' is false of every pre-merge head because the branch carries .legion/ handoffs.
findings.answer: C6 is judged on what lands on main (commits/M lists exactly the marker); the mid-run read is the pull request's file list filtered to non-.legion/LEGSMOKE-937/ paths and never 'exactly one file'.

findings.finding: Retro's docs/solutions/ learning would add a second path to the merged diff.
findings.answer: D7: no learning file under this Scope; learnings go in the retro Dispatch message; admitting a file is the architect's (section 8.4).

findings.finding: Retro's push must not carry skip-checks: true even though it only removes .legion/.
findings.answer: D11 classifies every push: handoff pushes trailered; the implementer's code pushes and retro's removal push are code pushes with no trailer, so check and gate run at R.

findings.finding: A driver-made .fail-me may sit on main, where the branch cannot cure it.
findings.answer: D10 and section 7.2: locate the file first (branch head and main); on the branch a deletion-only code commit; on main the implementer touches nothing and reports to the architect.

findings.finding: A .fail-me red is deterministic and not a rerun case.
findings.answer: D6 triage: read the failing run's log line; the .fail-me branch of gate is never rerun; any other failure gets the one rerun by the reviewer.

findings.finding: The required-check set must be re-derived at review time, not quoted from the plan.
findings.answer: D6 gives merge-gate.md's command verbatim for each round, the 12:40Z snapshot as the expected shape only, a per-round ruleset read for C3's no-bypass clause, and the PR opened right after the code push so pull_request runs exist.

findings.finding: The Scope's optional 'one more line' arm is unspecified in text, timing and effect on the criteria.
findings.answer: D4-D5 and C5: detector K or the driver's fenced line (KD=1), at most one line, the two-line literal and size computed from the extracted L; a post-approval request is a new round and its cost is the driver's; section 8.5.

findings.finding: Docs-only or not decides whether a simplify pass and the thermonuclear pair run.
findings.answer: D13 declares the diff docs-only: no ce-simplify-code, no Thermo line, no pair unless the driver asks.

findings.finding: The PR body needs a literal Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-937 line the template lacks.
findings.answer: D16 spells the body: the template sections plus the standalone Dispatch line, the CI line shape for ci/check and fail-on-demand/gate, Size, Chain, Fast-follow, and the jq checks that read them.

findings.finding: The upgrade rehearsal's relaunch semantics are not in the phase steps.
findings.answer: D14 and section 7.9: on relaunch re-read the record, issue and handoffs, re-derive from legion/LEGSMOKE-937@origin and GitHub, skip creation when the exact bytes are already at the remote head, call handoff_complete again rather than writing a second handoff, and quote any HANDOFF_* refusal verbatim.

findings.finding: The WAITING / sleep 300 gating is ambiguous about which roles it binds.
findings.answer: D14 states it per role: every role replies WAITING on its task line and acts on the driver's targeted message; only the implementer sleeps 300 (implementing and retro task lines, not the production check); the operator's hold overrides proceed-by-default.

findings.finding: The tester has no application, no harness and no red test to write.
findings.answer: Section 5.3: the tester re-runs the implementer's commands and drives the surface a second way through the git object API (trees, blobs, hash-object), lists its break attempts, and writes no test because the repository has no suite (D13).

findings.finding: The plan artifact is two objects and plan.json has four required records.
findings.answer: Section 9: plan.md uploaded as the issue artifact before plan.json is committed; planReview by the read-only plan-reviewer in the planner's session; specDepartures [] with its reading.

findings.finding: Concurrent sibling trees will move main under this PR; that is not a reason to merge the base in.
findings.answer: D19: a moved main needs nothing (strict policy false, disjoint paths); a forward merge only on a real CONFLICTING state; D0 rules out a path collision.
